records.title: Blower Motor Resistor Failure / Cowl Water Leak (HVAC Only Works on High)
records.description: A very common HHR HVAC fault: the blower fan stops working on low and medium speeds and only runs on High (which bypasses the resistor). The root cause is a failed blower motor resistor, frequently accelerated by a design flaw where the butyl sealant patch under the passenger-side cowl dries out and lets rainwater leak onto the blower motor and resistor. The wiring connector can melt as well, causing repeat failures.
records.solution: Replace the blower motor resistor (accessible in the passenger footwell) and inspect/replace the connector if it shows heat damage. Reseal the cowl butyl patch to stop water intrusion onto the HVAC components and prevent recurrence.
symptoms: Fan only blows on the highest speed setting
No air on low/medium fan speeds
Blower stops working entirely
Burning smell or melted blower connector
Water/dampness in passenger footwell

records.title: Defective Ignition Switch Can Shut Off Engine While Driving (Major Recall)
records.description: The HHR was part of GM's massive ignition switch recall. The switch is not robust enough, so a heavy key chain or a bump from the driver's knee can jostle the key out of the 'run' position, shutting off the engine and cutting power to steering, brakes and airbags. With the engine off, airbags will not deploy in a crash. This defect was tied to dozens of deaths and led to recall campaigns 14V047 (2006-2007) and the broader 14V171/14V355 ignition-key-removal action covering 2006-2011.
records.solution: Have the recall performed free of charge at any Chevrolet dealer; the dealer replaces the ignition switch (and on the key-removal recall, replaces the ignition cylinder and re-cuts/reprograms keys). Until repaired, owners were advised to drive with only the key (no fobs or heavy chains) on the ring. Verify completion by VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup.
symptoms: Engine suddenly shuts off while driving
Loss of power steering and power brakes when engine cuts out
Dashboard warning lights flash before stall
Airbags fail to deploy in a crash
Key can be removed when not in Park

records.title: Ecotec Timing Chain Stretch / Tensioner Failure
records.description: The 2.2L (L61/LE5) and 2.4L Ecotec four-cylinders are prone to timing chain wear caused by failing plastic guides and weak tensioners, often aggravated by extended oil-change intervals or low oil. Because the engine is an interference design, a stretched chain that jumps time can let pistons strike valves and destroy the engine. The telltale sign is a rattling or scraping noise from the passenger side of the engine, especially on cold start, frequently accompanied by code P0008/P0017 for cam-to-crank correlation.
records.solution: Replace the complete timing kit (chain, guides, tensioner and sprockets), not just one part, using quality kits (Cloyes, Melling, INA). Address any oil-consumption issue and use full synthetic oil with shorter change intervals to prevent recurrence.
symptoms: Rattling or scraping noise from passenger side of engine on cold start
Check engine light with cam/crank correlation codes
Rough running or misfire
Engine may not start if chain has jumped time
Reduced power

records.title: Inaccurate / Fluctuating Fuel Gauge (Fuel Level Sensor)
records.description: HHR owners frequently report the fuel gauge reading incorrectly or bouncing around unpredictably while driving, sometimes stuck on empty or full. The cause is the fuel level sensor inside the tank: the contact fingers that slide across the resistor card wear out or get fouled by fuel deposits, sending an erratic signal to the gauge. Bad readings can also coincide with ABS/traction warnings due to shared wiring or BCM issues.
records.solution: Inspect the tank-top connector and harness for corrosion/loose wires first; if those are good, replace the fuel level sensor (commonly part of the fuel pump/sending-unit assembly). This restores accurate gauge readings.
symptoms: Fuel needle jumps around while driving
Gauge stuck on empty or full
Gauge reads inaccurately compared to actual fuel level
Occasional ABS/traction light with the gauge fault

records.title: Interior Door Handles Break Off
records.description: The HHR's interior door handles are cheap chrome-plated plastic that crack and snap off during normal use, leaving the door unable to be opened from inside. CarComplaints logged 23 reports for the 2006 model alone, at an average of ~94,600 miles. GM never recalled the handles; dealers historically quoted replacing the entire inner door panel (often $300-$500), though the handle alone can be replaced far more cheaply with aftermarket parts.
records.solution: Replace the failed inner door handle with an aftermarket metal-reinforced or OEM handle rather than the whole door panel. DIY replacement typically runs well under $100 in parts; budget more if a shop installs it.
symptoms: Inside door handle cracks or snaps off
Door cannot be opened from the interior
Handle feels loose or flimsy before failing
Must exit through another door or window

records.title: Passlock Anti-Theft System No-Start (Security Light)
records.description: The HHR uses GM's Passlock theft-deterrent system, and a failing Passlock sensor in the ignition lock cylinder commonly triggers a false theft condition. The 'Service Theft Deterrent System' message appears, the security light flashes, and the engine cranks but will not start (or will not crank), often intermittently. A weak battery or a worn lock cylinder/sensor are the usual culprits.
records.solution: Try the 10-minute (or 30-minute, 3-cycle) Passlock relearn: turn key to ON without starting until the security light stops flashing, then start. If it recurs, replace the Passlock sensor or ignition lock cylinder and perform the relearn; verify battery health first.
symptoms: Security/anti-theft light flashing
'Service Theft Deterrent System' message
Engine cranks but won't start
Intermittent no-start that clears after a wait
Gauges acting erratically during the fault

records.title: Sudden Loss of Electric Power Steering (EPS) Assist
records.description: The HHR's electric power steering motor can fail intermittently or completely, causing the steering to suddenly become very heavy while driving. Owners report the EPS shutting off under any condition, after which the wheel is extremely hard to turn until the engine is shut off and restarted to reset the system. GM recall 14V153 covered the 2009-2010 non-turbo cars and replaced the EPS motor, and a GM bulletin extended free EPS motor replacement (lifetime) to many 2006-2009 non-turbo HHRs; turbo models were excluded despite similar complaints.
records.solution: Check eligibility for recall 14V153 and the lifetime EPS-motor warranty bulletin at a GM dealer for free replacement; otherwise replace the failed EPS motor/steering column motor assembly. NHTSA logged 100+ HHR steering complaints, the most common HHR complaint category.
symptoms: Steering suddenly becomes very hard to turn
Power steering warning light illuminates
Loss of assist most noticeable at low speeds and parking
Assist returns only after engine restart
Clunking or notchy feel in the column

records.title: Transmission Shift Cable / Rollaway Recall and Harsh Shifting (4T65E)
records.description: GM recalled 276,729 model-year 2009 vehicles, including the HHR, because the transmission shift cable adjustment clip may not be fully engaged (recall 09V073). When it isn't, the gear indicated by the shifter can differ from the transmission's actual gear, letting a driver select 'Park' and remove the key while the car is not truly in Park, allowing a rollaway. Separately, the 4T65E automatic is reported to develop delayed/harsh shifts (a 'thump' or 'bang') from soft aluminum valve-body shift valves galling and sticking in their bores, sometimes storing P1811.
records.solution: Have the 09V073 recall performed free at a dealer (inspect and, if needed, replace the shift cable so the clip fully engages). For harsh/delayed shifting, service the valve body or rebuild the transmission; updated valve-body components address the sticking shift valves.
symptoms: Vehicle can roll away after shifting to Park and removing key
Gear indicator does not match actual gear
Delayed engagement followed by a hard thump/bang shift
Intermittent harsh shifting
Stored code P1811 without check-engine light

records.title: Interior and Exterior Door Handle Breakage Trapping Occupants
records.description: The Chevrolet HHR is notorious for door handles that snap off, both interior and exterior. Interior door handle breakage is particularly dangerous as it can trap occupants inside the vehicle. The handles are made of brittle plastic that becomes fragile with age and temperature cycling. In cold weather, the handles are especially prone to snapping. This issue affects all HHR model years but is most commonly reported on 2006-2008 models.
records.solution: Replace broken door handles with aftermarket metal replacement handles when available, or use updated GM part numbers. Interior handle replacement is relatively simple DIY ($20-$50 per handle). Keep a window breaker tool in the vehicle as a safety precaution in case both interior handles and window controls fail simultaneously.
symptoms: Door handle snaps when pulled
Handle feels loose or wobbly before breaking
Interior door handle cracks in cold weather
Unable to open door from inside the vehicle
Handle plastic visibly cracked or discolored

citations.title: HHR Door Handle and Common Problems - 1A Auto

communityRecommendations.content: Broken interior door handles can trap you inside the vehicle. Keep a window breaker tool accessible in the car. Replace handles proactively if they feel loose or show any cracking. Aftermarket metal handles are available and much more durable than the OEM plastic ones

records.title: Ecotec Timing Chain Tensioner Failure and Chain Stretch
records.description: The 2.2L and 2.4L Ecotec engines in the HHR suffer from timing chain tensioner failure and chain stretch, particularly on early production years. The timing chain tensioner does not receive sufficient oil at idle due to a design fault in early engines, causing accelerated wear. The 2.4L Ecotec is especially prone to this issue and also suffers from oil consumption problems. GM released revised tensioners and oil nozzles but many HHRs were never updated. Symptoms typically appear between 80,000-120,000 miles.
records.solution: Replace timing chain, tensioner (use revised GM part), guides, and sprockets as a complete kit. Do the water pump at the same time since it shares access. For the 2.4L, also address any oil consumption by checking the piston rings. Total repair cost is $800-$2,000 depending on engine and additional work needed.
symptoms: Rattling noise on cold start that may diminish when warm
Check engine light with P0017 camshaft position code
Engine running rough or misfiring
Reduced engine power under acceleration
Timing chain noise that progressively worsens

citations.title: GM 2.4 Ecotec Timing Chain Problem Explained

communityRecommendations.content: Use the GM revised timing chain tensioner (updated part number) when replacing. The original design had insufficient oil feed at idle causing premature failure. Always replace the complete kit - chain, tensioner, guides, and sprockets. Half-measures will result in repeat failure

The 2.4L Ecotec is worse than the 2.2L for timing chain issues and also burns oil. If you are spending $1,000+ on timing chain repair, consider the overall condition of the vehicle. A high-mileage HHR with a 2.4L may not be worth the investment

records.title: Fuel Line Corrosion and Leak Near Rear Wheel
records.description: The HHR has a documented issue with fuel line corrosion, particularly in rust belt states. The fuel line corrodes just forward of the driver-side rear wheel, developing leaks that create a fire hazard. Road salt and debris accelerate the corrosion. The issue is most commonly seen on vehicles in the northeastern and midwestern United States where road salt is used heavily in winter.
records.solution: Inspect fuel lines annually, especially near the driver-side rear wheel. If corrosion is found, replace the affected fuel line section with stainless steel or nylon-coated replacement lines. Do not use tape or sealant on fuel lines - full section replacement is required. Cost is $200-$500 at an independent shop.
symptoms: Gasoline smell near the vehicle
Visible fuel drip under vehicle near rear driver-side wheel
Fuel economy decreasing noticeably
Rust or corrosion visible on fuel lines during inspection
Check engine light with evaporative system codes

citations.title: HHR Fuel Line Corrosion Issue - ChevroletProblems.com

communityRecommendations.content: A leaking fuel line is an immediate fire hazard. If you smell gasoline or see fuel dripping, stop driving the vehicle until the line is repaired. This is especially common on HHRs in rust-belt states. Annual undercarriage inspection is essential for vehicles in areas with road salt

records.title: Defective Ignition Switch Causing Engine Shutoff and Airbag Failure
records.description: Every HHR from 2006 to 2011 was affected by GM's ignition switch recall. A heavy keyring or rough road conditions can shift the ignition from "Run" to "Accessory," shutting off the engine and disabling the airbags, power steering, and power brakes while driving. The GM victim compensation fund paid out for 77 deaths and 141 injuries related to this defect across all affected GM vehicles. The defect is identical to the Cobalt ignition switch issue.
records.solution: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls for recall eligibility. The recall remedy is ignition switch replacement, free of charge at any GM dealer. Until repaired, remove everything from your keychain except the ignition key. If the engine shuts off while driving, shift to Neutral and steer to safety.
symptoms: Engine shuts off unexpectedly while driving
Loss of power steering and power brakes simultaneously
Airbag warning light illuminated
Key turns to accessory position without driver input
Vehicle stalls on rough roads or when key bumped

records.title: Electric Power Steering Sudden Loss of Assist
records.description: The HHR uses an electric power steering system that is prone to sudden failure, particularly on 2006-2008 models. The power steering can quit mid-drive with no warning, making the vehicle extremely difficult to steer. The 2007 model alone logged 550+ NHTSA complaints and was involved in 17 crashes related to this and other issues. The EPS module failure is the most dangerous of the HHR's common problems.
records.solution: Replace the electric power steering motor/module. Check for recall eligibility as some model years are covered. If power steering fails while driving, reduce speed immediately and use both hands to steer. The vehicle is still steerable but requires significant effort. Replacement costs $400-$800 including labor.
symptoms: Complete loss of power steering assist while driving
Power steering warning light illuminated
Steering becomes extremely heavy suddenly
Intermittent power steering assist
Groaning or whining noise from steering column
